name: Wellspring Worldwide
tagline: Enterprise software for managing invention disclosures, patents, licensing deals and innovation pipelines, aimed at university tech transfer offices and corporate R&D.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Wellspring sells through enterprise contracts and does not publish list pricing.

verdictSummary: This is not an app you replace, it is a system of record for someone else's legal obligations. The schema part is boring: disclosures, inventors, patent families, agreements, royalty splits, deadlines. The part that cannot be one-shot is everything attached to that schema: docket feeds from patent offices, outside counsel workflows, royalty distribution that survives an audit, and the institutional data that has been accumulating in it since before you arrived. Also, nobody buys this for themselves. A solo person with ideas to track needs a notes app, not an IP management platform, and the honest build below is exactly that.
coreLoopDIY: A local tracker for your own inventions, filings and deadlines: one row per idea, linked patent numbers, renewal dates, and a dashboard of what is due in the next ninety days.
requirements: Manual entry of patent and application numbers
Optional USPTO or EPO public API key if you want status lookups
whatYouLose: Patent office docketing feeds and automated status changes, so every deadline is one you typed in yourself
Royalty and revenue distribution math that an auditor will accept
Outside counsel and inventor portals, plus the permission model that keeps them apart
Agreement and obligation tracking across thousands of contracts with reporting that a dean or CFO will read
Any record of the fifteen years of institutional history already sitting in the vendor's database
moatNotes: The acquisition pattern here is the tell: buying IP data and advisory shops folds more hard-to-replicate corpus into the product rather than more features.
whyPeopleStillPay: Tech transfer offices and corporate IP teams are not paying for a database, they are paying for someone to be accountable when a renewal deadline is missed and a patent goes abandoned. That accountability comes bundled with docket integrations, audit trails, royalty distribution reporting and a vendor who will answer the phone during an audit. Migration is also brutal: the existing records are the office's entire history of ownership and obligation, and moving them means re-verifying thousands of legal relationships. Nobody volunteers for that to save a line item.
notes: A personal IP tracker is a weekend of work and genuinely useful if you file your own patents. The moat is not the form fields, it is the docket feeds, the audit-grade royalty records, and decades of institutional filings that nobody is migrating out by hand.
prompt:
Build a local, single-user IP and invention tracker. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Next.js 15 with the app router and TypeScript
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/ip.db, schema created on first run
- Tailwind for styling, no component library
- Runs with `npm run dev` on localhost only

Data model:
- invention: id, title, short description, disclosure date, status (idea, disclosed, filed, granted, abandoned, licensed), notes markdown
- filing: id, invention_id, jurisdiction, kind (provisional, utility, PCT, design), application number, filing date, publication number, grant number, status
- deadline: id, filing_id, label, due date, done boolean
- contact: id, name, role (co-inventor, attorney, licensee), email, notes
- link table between invention and contact
- attachment: id, invention_id, file path relative to ./data/files, original filename

Features, in scope:
- CRUD for all of the above with plain server actions and forms, no client state library
- Dashboard: deadlines due in the next 90 days sorted ascending, overdue ones flagged red, count of inventions by status
- Invention detail page showing filings, deadlines, linked contacts, attachments, markdown notes rendered
- Full text search across invention titles, descriptions and notes using SQLite FTS5
- File upload that copies into ./data/files and stores the path, no size limit handling beyond a 25MB guard
- Export everything to a single JSON file and a zip of ./data on demand
- Seed script with three fake inventions so the UI is not empty on first load

Explicitly out of scope, do not build:
- Any patent office API integration, docketing automation or status polling
- Multi-user auth, roles, inventor portals or sharing
- Royalty calculation, revenue splits or accounting reports
- Email reminders; the dashboard is the reminder

Other rules:
- Any config goes in .env, read via process.env, with a .env.example committed and .env gitignored
- Gitignore ./data entirely
- README with setup in under ten lines and one paragraph stating plainly that this tracks deadlines you type in yourself and is not a system of record for anything legally binding
